summary: Implement Proxy [[Delete]] via deleteProperty trap with non-configurable and non-extensible target invariants.

target.notes: Validate revocation, perform GetMethod trap lookup, call the trap with handler as this, then enforce the ECMAScript Proxy invariant before returning.

semantics.invariants: truthy result cannot report deletion of a non-configurable own property or any still-existing own property of a non-extensible target

caveats: If the trap is absent/undefined, forward to the corresponding target internal method.
Trap property lookup itself can invoke a getter and throw.
A C# interceptor that trusts the trap result without target invariant checks is not semantics-preserving.

tests.name: configurable property can be deleted by forwarding trap
tests.input: const t={x:1};const p=new Proxy(t,{deleteProperty(t,k){return Reflect.deleteProperty(t,k)}});console.log(Reflect.deleteProperty(p,'x'),'x' in t);

tests.name: non-extensible existing property cannot be faked deleted
tests.input: const t={x:1};Object.preventExtensions(t);const p=new Proxy(t,{deleteProperty(){return true}});try{Reflect.deleteProperty(p,'x')}catch(e){console.log(e instanceof TypeError)}
